problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡t+2t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{t}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡t+4{cos}^{2}⁡t-2t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{t}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+{t}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}}⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
